newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Elf hits potentially large Angola oilfield.
newsitem.headline: Elf hits potentially large Angola oilfield.

text.p: Operator Elf Aquitaine SA has found a potentially large oilfield in a block off the coast of Angola, a senior official at a company which is a partner in the field said Monday.
"There has been a new discovery in Block 17," the oil company official, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters. "The initial indications are that it is a very big field."
Oil industry analysts in Luanda also said early information pointed to a large field, though they added that it was too early to confirm industry rumor that it was a billion barrels.

"This was in the Dalia field in Block 17. There is some big excitement about it but it is too early to say for sure how big it is," said a usually well-informed industry analyst, who also asked not to be quoted by name.
Elf officials in Luanda had no comment on the discovery Monday but said a statement will be issued on Tuesday because of the speculation.

Elf Exploration, a joint venture between the French oil company Elf Aquitaine and the Angolan state oil company Sonangol, is the operator of the Block 17 drilling licence and holds a 35 percent stake in the block.
Other partners in Block 17 are Esso Exploration Angola, BP Exploration (Angola), Den Norske Stats Oljeselkskap ASA (Statoil), Norsk Hydro and Fina Exploration M.B.V.
